# Introduction


- Consider:
$$
y = X\beta + u
$$
  - $y \in \R^n$
  - $X \in \R^{n \times k}$, nonstochastic
  - $\Er[u] = 0$, $\Er[uu'] = \sigma^2 I_n$

- $\hat{\beta} = (X'X)^{-1}X'y$ is linear in $y$ and unbiased

::: {.fragment}

- If $\tilde{\beta}$ is another estimator linear in $y$ and unbiased, how does its variance compare to $\hat{\beta}$?

:::

## Gauss-Markov Theorem


:::{.callout-warning icon=false}

### Theorem: Gauss-Markov

If $\Er[u] = 0$ and $\Er[uu'] = \sigma^2 I_n$, then the best linear unbiased estimator (BLUE) of
$a'\beta = a'\hat{\beta}$ where $\hat{\beta} = (X'X)^{-1} X'y$

:::

::: {.fragment}

- This chapter: use linear algebra to further understand and generalize this result

:::


# Projection Geometry and Quadratic Forms

## Linear Subspaces

- $V \subseteq \R^n$, **complete inner product space** (Hilbert space)
- $L \subset V$ a subspace

::: {.callout-tip icon=false}

### Definition

An $L \subset V$ is a **subspace** if $\forall x, y \in L$, $\alpha,
\beta \in \R$, $\alpha x + \beta y \in L$

:::

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
using Plots, LaTeXStrings

p = plot(xlims=(-3.2, 3.5), ylims=(-2.2, 2.2), aspect_ratio=:equal,
         framestyle=:origin, grid=true, gridalpha=0.3,
         legend=false, size=(600, 320))
plot!(p, [-3, 3], [-1.5, 1.5], lw=2.5, color=:steelblue)
annotate!(p, 3.1, 1.6, text(L"L", 11, :steelblue, :left))
plot!(p, [0, 1.2], [0, 0.6], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:blue)
annotate!(p, 1.25, 0.45, text(L"x \in L", 10, :blue, :left))
plot!(p, [0, -1.0], [0, -0.5], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:teal)
annotate!(p, -1.05, -0.65, text(L"y \in L", 10, :teal, :right))
plot!(p, [0, 2.0], [0, 1.0], arrow=true, lw=2, linestyle=:dash, color=:crimson)
annotate!(p, 2.05, 0.85, text(L"\alpha x + \beta y \in L", 10, :crimson, :left))
scatter!(p, [0], [0], color=:black, markersize=3)
p
```

## Orthogonal Subspaces


::: {.callout-tip icon=false}

### Definition

Given a subspace $L \subset V$ **the orthogonal complement** of $L$ is
$$
L^\perp = \{x \in V: x' l = 0 \,\forall l \in L\}
$$

:::

- For any $y \in V$,  $\exists y_1 \in L$, $y_2 \in L^\perp$ s.t.
$y = y_1 + y_2$

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
using Plots, LaTeXStrings

p = plot(xlims=(-3.2, 3.5), ylims=(-3.2, 3.5), aspect_ratio=:equal,
         framestyle=:origin, grid=true, gridalpha=0.3,
         legend=false, size=(600, 320))
plot!(p, [-3, 3], [-1.5, 1.5], lw=2.5, color=:steelblue)
annotate!(p, 3.1, 1.6, text(L"L", 11, :steelblue, :left))
plot!(p, [-1.5, 1.5], [3, -3], lw=2.5, color=:coral)
annotate!(p, -1.5, 3.2, text(L"L^\perp", 11, :coral, :center))

plot!(p, [0, 1.8], [0, 0.9], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:blue)
annotate!(p, 1.85, 0.75, text(L"y_1 \in L", 10, :blue, :left))
plot!(p, [0, -0.8], [0, 1.6], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:red)
annotate!(p, -0.9, 1.7, text(L"y_2 \in L^\perp", 10, :red, :right))
plot!(p, [0, 1.0], [0, 2.5], arrow=true, lw=3, color=:purple)
annotate!(p, 1.05, 2.7, text(L"y = y_1 + y_2", 11, :purple, :left))

plot!(p, [1.8, 1.0], [0.9, 2.5], linestyle=:dash, color=:gray)
plot!(p, [-0.8, 1.0], [1.6, 2.5], linestyle=:dash, color=:gray)
p
```

## Orthogonal and Sums of Subspaces

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.callout-warning icon=false}

### Lemma 1.1

Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be subspaces of $V$, then
$$
(\underbrace{L_1 + L_2}_{\{l_1 + l_2 \in V:  l_1 \in L_2, l_2 \in L_2\}})^\perp = L_1^\perp \cap L_2^\perp
$$
and
$$
(L_1 \cap L_2)^\perp = L_1^\perp + L_2^\perp
$$

:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
using Plots, LaTeXStrings

xg = -2.0:1.0:2.0
yg = -2.0:1.0:2.0
zg = zeros(length(xg), length(yg))

p = plot(camera=(35, 25), legend=false, size=(420, 420))
surface!(p, xg, yg, zg, alpha=0.3, color=:blues, colorbar=false)
plot!(p, [-2.2, 2.2], [0, 0], [0, 0], lw=3, color=:blue)
plot!(p, [0, 0], [-2.2, 2.2], [0, 0], lw=3, color=:teal)
plot!(p, [0, 0], [0, 0], [-2.2, 2.2], lw=3.5, color=:crimson)
plot!(p, [0, 1.5], [0, 0], [0, 0], arrow=true, lw=3, color=:darkblue)
plot!(p, [0, 0], [0, 1.5], [0, 0], arrow=true, lw=3, color=:darkgreen)
plot!(p, [0, 0], [0, 0], [0, 1.8], arrow=true, lw=3.5, color=:red)

annotate!(p, -1.2, 1.5, 0.1, text(L"L_1 + L_2", 10, :steelblue, :center))
annotate!(p, 2.3, 0.0, 0.0, text(L"L_1", 10, :blue, :left))
annotate!(p, 0.0, 2.3, 0.0, text(L"L_2", 10, :teal, :left))
annotate!(p, 0.0, 0.0, 2.4, text(L"(L_1+L_2)^\perp = L_1^\perp \cap L_2^\perp", 10, :crimson, :center))
p
```

:::

## Projection

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.callout-tip icon=false}

### Definition

$P_L y \in  L$ is the **projection** of $y$ on $L$ if
$$
\norm{y - P_L y } = \inf_{w \in L} \norm{y - w}
$$

:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
using Plots, LaTeXStrings, LinearAlgebra

p = plot(xlims=(-0.5, 4.3), ylims=(-0.5, 3.2), aspect_ratio=:equal,
         framestyle=:none, legend=false, size=(320, 320))

# Subspace L
plot!(p, [-0.5, 4.2], [-0.2, 1.68], lw=2.5, color=:steelblue)
annotate!(p, 4.2, 1.8, text(L"L", 11, :steelblue, :left))

# Vector y and projection py = P_L y
py = [2.155, 0.862]
y = [1.5, 2.5]
w = [3.6, 1.44]

plot!(p, [0, y[1]], [0, y[2]], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:purple)
annotate!(p, 0.65, 1.45, text(L"y", 11, :purple, :right))

plot!(p, [0, py[1]], [0, py[2]], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:blue)
annotate!(p, 2.2, 0.6, text(L"P_L y", 11, :blue, :left))

# Residual y - P_L y (orthogonal to L)
plot!(p, [py[1], y[1]], [py[2], y[2]], lw=2.5, linestyle=:dash, color=:crimson)
annotate!(p, 1.95, 1.85, text(L"y - P_L y \perp L", 10, :crimson, :left))

# Arbitrary point w in L
scatter!(p, [w[1]], [w[2]], color=:darkgreen, markersize=4)
annotate!(p, 3.65, 1.25, text(L"w \in L", 10, :darkgreen, :left))
plot!(p, [y[1], w[1]], [y[2], w[2]], lw=1.5, linestyle=:dot, color=:darkgreen)
annotate!(p, 2.8, 2.2, text(L"\Vert y - w \Vert", 9, :darkgreen, :left))

# Right angle symbol at py
d_res = (y - py) ./ norm(y - py) .* 0.2
d_L = (-py) ./ norm(py) .* 0.2
corner = py + d_res + d_L
plot!(p, [py[1] + d_L[1], corner[1], py[1] + d_res[1]],
         [py[2] + d_L[2], corner[2], py[2] + d_res[2]], color=:black, lw=1.2)
p
```

:::

:::::

:::{.fragment}

:::{.callout-warning icon=false}

### Projection Theorem

1. $P_L y$ exists, is unique, and is a linear function of $y$

2. For any $y_1^* \in L$, $y_1^* = P_L y$ iff $y- y_1^* \perp L$

:::

- 2 implies if $y = y_1 + y_2$ with $y_1 \in L$ and $y_2 \in L^\perp$,
then $y_1 = P_L y$

:::



## Projection Map

:::{.callout-warning icon=false}

### Theorem 1.2

A linear map $G: V \to L$ is the projection map onto $L$ iff $Gy = y$
$\forall y \in L$ and $Gy = 0$ $\forall y \in L^\perp$
:::

## Projection Map

:::{.callout-tip icon=false}

### Definition

Linear $G: V \to V$ is

- **idempotent** if $G (G y) =  G y$ $\forall y \in V$

- **symmetric** if $G'y = G y$ $\forall y \in V$
:::

:::{.callout-warning icon=false}

### Theorem 1.3

A linear map $G: V \to V$ is a projection map onto its range, $\mathcal{R}(G)$, iff $G$ is idempotent and symmetric.

:::

## Projection Differences

:::{.callout-warning icon=false}

### Theorem 1.4

Let $L \subset V$ and $L_0 \subset L$ be subspaces. Then
$P_L - P_{L_0} = P_{L \cap L_0^\perp}$

:::

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
using Plots, LaTeXStrings

xg = -0.5:1.0:3.5
yg = -0.5:1.0:3.5
zg = zeros(length(xg), length(yg))

p = plot(camera=(35, 30), legend=false, size=(600, 320))
surface!(p, xg, yg, zg, alpha=0.25, color=:blues, colorbar=false)
annotate!(p, 3.2, 0.2, 0.05, text(L"L", 11, :steelblue))

plot!(p, [0, 3.5], [0, 0], [0, 0], lw=3, color=:blue)
annotate!(p, 3.6, 0.0, 0.0, text(L"L_0", 11, :blue, :left))

plot!(p, [0, 0], [0, 3.5], [0, 0], lw=3, color=:teal)
annotate!(p, 0.0, 3.6, 0.0, text(L"L \cap L_0^\perp", 11, :teal, :left))

y = [2.2, 2.5, 2.2]
py_L = [2.2, 2.5, 0.0]
py_L0 = [2.2, 0.0, 0.0]
py_diff = [0.0, 2.5, 0.0]

plot!(p, [0, y[1]], [0, y[2]], [0, y[3]], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:purple)
annotate!(p, y[1], y[2], y[3] + 0.25, text(L"y", 11, :purple, :center))

plot!(p, [0, py_L[1]], [0, py_L[2]], [0, py_L[3]], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:navy)
annotate!(p, py_L[1] + 0.2, py_L[2] + 0.2, 0.0, text(L"P_L y", 11, :navy, :left))

plot!(p, [0, py_L0[1]], [0, py_L0[2]], [0, py_L0[3]], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:blue)
annotate!(p, py_L0[1], -0.3, 0.0, text(L"P_{L_0} y", 10, :blue, :center))

plot!(p, [0, py_diff[1]], [0, py_diff[2]], [0, py_diff[3]], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:teal)
annotate!(p, -0.3, py_diff[2], 0.0, text(L"P_{L \cap L_0^\perp} y", 10, :teal, :right))

plot!(p, [py_L0[1], py_L[1]], [py_L0[2], py_L[2]], [py_L0[3], py_L[3]], lw=2, linestyle=:dash, color=:teal)
plot!(p, [py_diff[1], py_L[1]], [py_diff[2], py_L[2]], [py_diff[3], py_L[3]], lw=1.5, linestyle=:dot, color=:gray)

plot!(p, [py_L[1], y[1]], [py_L[2], y[2]], [py_L[3], y[3]], lw=2, linestyle=:dash, color=:crimson)
annotate!(p, py_L[1] + 0.1, py_L[2] + 0.1, 1.1, text(L"y - P_L y", 10, :crimson, :left))

p
```

## Projection onto $X$

::: {.callout-tip icon=false}

### Definition

For linear $H: \R^s \to \R^r$, the **g-inverse** of $H$ is any $H^{-}$
s.t. $H H^{-} H = H$

:::

:::{.fragment}

:::{.callout-warning icon=false}

### Theorem 1.5

Let $X: \R^k \to \R^n$ be linear. The projection onto $\mathcal{R}(X)$
is $P_X = X(X'X)^- X'$ where $(X'X)^{-}$ is any g-inverse of $X'X$

:::

:::

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
using Plots, LaTeXStrings, LinearAlgebra

x1 = [2.0, 0.3, 0.0]
x2 = [0.5, 1.8, 0.0]
X = [x1 x2]

y = [1.8, 2.2, 2.0]
beta_hat = (X'*X) \ (X'*y)
py = X * beta_hat
b1x1 = beta_hat[1] * x1
b2x2 = beta_hat[2] * x2

xg = -0.5:1.0:3.5
yg = -0.5:1.0:3.5
zg = zeros(length(xg), length(yg))

p = plot(camera=(35, 28), legend=false, size=(600, 320))
surface!(p, xg, yg, zg, alpha=0.22, color=:blues, colorbar=false)
annotate!(p, 3.2, 0.3, 0.05, text(L"\mathcal{R}(X)", 11, :steelblue))

plot!(p, [0, x1[1]], [0, x1[2]], [0, x1[3]], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:darkblue)
annotate!(p, x1[1] + 0.15, x1[2], 0.0, text(L"x_1", 11, :darkblue, :left))

plot!(p, [0, x2[1]], [0, x2[2]], [0, x2[3]], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:darkgreen)
annotate!(p, x2[1], x2[2] + 0.2, 0.0, text(L"x_2", 11, :darkgreen, :center))

plot!(p, [0, b1x1[1]], [0, b1x1[2]], [0, b1x1[3]], lw=1.8, linestyle=:dash, color=:darkblue)
plot!(p, [0, b2x2[1]], [0, b2x2[2]], [0, b2x2[3]], lw=1.8, linestyle=:dash, color=:darkgreen)
plot!(p, [b1x1[1], py[1]], [b1x1[2], py[2]], [b1x1[3], py[3]], lw=1.2, linestyle=:dot, color=:gray)
plot!(p, [b2x2[1], py[1]], [b2x2[2], py[2]], [b2x2[3], py[3]], lw=1.2, linestyle=:dot, color=:gray)

plot!(p, [0, py[1]], [0, py[2]], [0, py[3]], arrow=true, lw=3, color=:blue)
annotate!(p, py[1] + 0.2, py[2] + 0.1, 0.0, text(L"P_X y = X\hat{\beta}", 11, :blue, :left))

plot!(p, [0, y[1]], [0, y[2]], [0, y[3]], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:purple)
annotate!(p, y[1], y[2], y[3] + 0.25, text(L"y", 11, :purple, :center))

plot!(p, [py[1], y[1]], [py[2], y[2]], [py[3], y[3]], lw=2.5, linestyle=:dash, color=:crimson)
annotate!(p, py[1] + 0.1, py[2] + 0.1, 1.0, text(L"y - P_X y \perp \mathcal{R}(X)", 10, :crimson, :left))

p
```

## Projection Spectrum

:::{.callout-tip icon=false}

### Definition

Let $A: V \to V$ be linear. Then $\lambda$ is an **eigenvalue**  of $A$  and $v \neq 0$ is an associated **eigenvector** if
$A v = \lambda v$

:::

:::{.notes}

Existence of (possibly complex) eigenvalues as roots of characteristic polynomial

:::

:::{.callout-warning icon=false}

### Lemma 1.2

The eigenvalues of a symmetric and idempotent matrix, $P$ are either $0$ or $1$. Furthmore rank of $P$ is the sum of its eigenvalues.

:::

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
using Plots, LaTeXStrings

p = plot(xlims=(-3.2, 3.5), ylims=(-3.2, 3.5), aspect_ratio=:equal,
         framestyle=:origin, grid=true, gridalpha=0.3,
         legend=false, size=(600, 320))

plot!(p, [-3, 3], [-1.5, 1.5], lw=2.5, color=:steelblue)
annotate!(p, 3.1, 1.6, text(L"E_{\lambda=1} = L", 10, :steelblue, :left))

plot!(p, [-1.5, 1.5], [3, -3], lw=2.5, color=:coral)
annotate!(p, -1.4, 3.2, text(L"E_{\lambda=0} = L^\perp", 10, :coral, :center))

plot!(p, [0, 1.8], [0, 0.9], arrow=true, lw=3, color=:blue)
annotate!(p, 1.85, 0.65, text(L"v_1 : P v_1 = 1 \cdot v_1", 10, :blue, :left))

plot!(p, [0, -0.8], [0, 1.6], arrow=true, lw=3, color=:red)
annotate!(p, -0.9, 1.8, text(L"v_0 : P v_0 = 0", 10, :red, :right))

plot!(p, [-0.75, -0.1], [1.5, 0.2], arrow=true, lw=1.5, linestyle=:dash, color=:darkred)
annotate!(p, -0.15, 0.85, text(L"P v_0 = 0", 9, :darkred, :left))

scatter!(p, [0], [0], color=:black, markersize=3)
p
```

## Projection Rank

:::{.callout-warning icon=false}

### Theorem 1.6

1. $\mathrm{rank}(P_X) = \mathrm{rank}(X)$

2. $\rank(I-P_X) = n - \rank(X)$

:::

# Generalized Linear Model

## Generalized Linear Model

$$
Y = \theta + u
$$

-  $\theta \in L \subset \R^n$, $L$ a known subspace

-  $u \in \R^n$ unobserved

:::{.fragment}
- Example:
$$
Y_i = x_{i,1} \beta_1 + \cdots + x_{i,k} \beta_k + u_i
$$
    - $X_k \equiv (x_{1,k}, ... , x_{n,k})'$, $X \equiv(X_1, ...,  X_k)$, $\beta \equiv (\beta_1, ..., \beta_k)'$,
      $y \equiv (Y_1, ..., Y_n)'$, $u \equiv (u_1, ..., u_n)'$
    $$y= X\beta + u$$
    fits setup with $L = \mathcal{R}(X)$
:::

## Least-Squares

- $\hat{\theta} = P_L y$, i.e. $\norm{y - \hat{\theta} y }^2 = \inf_{w \in L} \norm{y - w}^2$

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
using Plots, LaTeXStrings, LinearAlgebra

p = plot(xlims=(-0.5, 4.3), ylims=(-0.5, 3.2), aspect_ratio=:equal,
         framestyle=:none, legend=false, size=(600, 320))

plot!(p, [-0.5, 4.2], [-0.2, 1.68], lw=2.5, color=:steelblue)
annotate!(p, 4.2, 1.8, text(L"L", 11, :steelblue, :left))

theta = [1.5, 0.6]
y = [1.2, 2.4]
py = (dot(y, [1.0, 0.4]) / 1.16) .* [1.0, 0.4]

plot!(p, [0, theta[1]], [0, theta[2]], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:darkgreen)
annotate!(p, theta[1] - 0.2, theta[2] - 0.2, text(L"\theta \in L}", 10, :darkgreen, :right))

plot!(p, [theta[1], y[1]], [theta[2], y[2]], arrow=true, lw=2, linestyle=:dash, color=:orange)
annotate!(p, (theta[1] + y[1])/2 - 0.15, (theta[2] + y[2])/2, text(L"u}", 10, :orange, :right))

plot!(p, [0, y[1]], [0, y[2]], arrow=true, lw=2.5, color=:purple)
annotate!(p, y[1] - 0.1, y[2] + 0.15, text(L"y = \theta + u", 11, :purple, :right))

plot!(p, [0, py[1]], [0, py[2]], arrow=true, lw=3, color=:blue)
annotate!(p, py[1] + 0.2, py[2] - 0.2, text(L"\hat{\theta} = P_L y", 11, :blue, :left))

plot!(p, [py[1], y[1]], [py[2], y[2]], lw=2.5, linestyle=:dash, color=:crimson)
annotate!(p, (py[1] + y[1])/2 + 0.15, (py[2] + y[2])/2 + 0.15, text(L"y - \hat{\theta} \perp L", 10, :crimson, :left))

d_res = (y - py) ./ norm(y - py) .* 0.2
d_L = (-py) ./ norm(py) .* 0.2
corner = py + d_res + d_L
plot!(p, [py[1] + d_L[1], corner[1], py[1] + d_res[1]],
         [py[2] + d_L[2], corner[2], py[2] + d_res[2]], color=:black, lw=1.2)

p
```


# Gauss-Markov Theorem

## Gauss-Markov Theorem

:::{.callout-warning icon=false}

### Theorem: Gauss-Markov

If $\Er[u] = 0$ and $\Er[uu'] = \sigma^2 I_n$, then the best linear unbiased estimator (BLUE) of
$a'\theta = a'\hat{\theta}$ where $\hat{\theta} = P_L y$

:::


:::{.fragment}

:::{.callout-warning icon=false}

### Corollary

If
$$
y = X'\beta + u
$$
and $\Er[u] = 0$ and $\Er[uu'] = \sigma^2 I_n$, then the BLUE of $c'\beta$ is $c'\hat{\beta}$ with $\hat{\beta} =
(X'X)^{-1} X' y$

:::

:::
